did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 10 opens by showing how a child’s character affects the parents: a wise son makes his father glad, while a foolish son brings grief to his mother.

Did you know? The wise person in this chapter is not merely knowledgeable, but also acts at the right time: he gathers crops in summer, while the one who sleeps during the harvest is described as a disgraceful son.
Did you know? The chapter contrasts the memory of the righteous, which becomes a blessing, with the name of the wicked, which is described as decaying and disappearing.
Did you know? According to this verse, practical wisdom is shown by accepting commandments, while foolish speech can lead a person into trouble.
Did you know? Proverbs contrasts hatred, which stirs up conflict, with love, which covers offenses and prevents strife from spreading.
Did you know? The chapter warns that an abundance of words can involve an abundance of sin, and presents restraint from unnecessary speech as a sign of wisdom.
Did you know? This verse attributes wealth to the Lord’s blessing and emphasizes that this blessing does not come with sorrow.
Did you know? The wicked and the righteous are described in opposite ways after a storm: the wicked pass away and are gone, while the righteous remain as an everlasting foundation.
Did you know? The fear of the Lord is presented in this chapter as a way of adding days to one’s life, in contrast to the shortened years of the wicked.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the mouth of the righteous is described as a source of wisdom, while a perverse tongue will be cut off; in this way, a person’s speech reflects their moral character.
